title: A wrong fact is never polish
statement: A wrong fact in the text, the key or any line a student reads is never a polish note: it holds the item back until fixed.
example: Of 24 minor findings in one review, the 4 lines untrue to the story were fixed and the rest left as polish.
detail: A Grade 3 demonstration unit sends every world claim in its passages to an independent factuality pass: any failed or unresolved claim holds the text as a draft, and a wrong world claim in a child's science text is a kill, not a footnote. A later review register of four lessons acted on minor findings only when a line was untrue to the story, folding those into the fix batch, and listed a find-it key that taught a fact not in the story among its serious fixes. A wrong fact holds the item back however good the rest of it is, and it is never a footnote either.

evidence.quote: Any FAIL or unresolved verdict HOLDS THAT TEXT as a draft
A wrong world claim in a child's science text is a kill, not a footnote.
POLISH (recorded, not acted on unless a line is untrue to the story)
Untrue-to-story lines among them, folded into the FIX batch
find-it key teaches a fact not in the story
It is a factual-grounding and attribution problem, not a disagreement about elegant wording.
